description: This case study is the Delta Programme's page on flood risk management in the Netherlands, where a third of the country lies below sea level and, without dikes, dunes and storm surge barriers, 60 percent would be regularly inundated, an area with about nine million people and around 70 percent of GDP. It explains that flood risk management is one of the programme's three themes, that the Delta Decision and preferred regional strategies of 2015 were set out in the 2016 to 2021 National Water Plan, that the Sand Decision covers natural protection with sand, and that the 2022 to 2027 National Water Programme is the successor. The policy has moved to a flood risk approach that links the protection level to both the probability of flooding and the consequences, and the Flood Protection Programme is the multi-year implementation in which water authorities and Rijkswaterstaat upgrade dikes in an alliance. Coverage: national policy narrative with headline figures, not a dataset. Access: free web page in English; licence not stated. Caveats: a programme summary with limited method detail, and the Dutch-language programme documents carry more. It informs adaptation pathway, protection standard and dike upgrade simulations, and lists no linked catalogue records.
